outcomes.text: Use Spanish to talk about identity, family, friends and relationships with others.
Use Spanish to talk about healthy living, food, exercise and lifestyle habits.
Use Spanish to discuss school, studies, jobs and future work plans.
Use Spanish to talk about hobbies, sport, music and other free-time activities.
Describe customs, festivals and celebrations in Spanish-speaking communities.
Discuss famous people and celebrity culture in Spanish.

topics.title: 3.1.3 Theme 3: Communication and the world around us

outcomes.text: Use Spanish to talk about travel, holidays, tourism and places of interest.
Discuss media, social networks and technology in Spanish.
Talk about the environment, towns, regions and where people live in Spanish.

subtopics.title: Using themes across all four skills

outcomes.text: Apply the prescribed vocabulary and grammar across listening, speaking, reading and writing tasks in all themes.
Know that Foundation grammar is required receptively and productively, and Higher tier includes all Foundation grammar.
Understand that derivational word formation is only tested in the Reading paper.
Form feminine nouns: -o to -a, add -a to -or, no change for -ante/-ente/-ista.
Form plurals: add -s after a vowel, -es after a consonant, -z to -ces, and drop the accent from -ión nouns.
Use the infinitive as a noun, like the English -ing form.
Use a language name as a masculine noun, and nationality adjectives as nouns.
Make definite and indefinite articles agree with their noun, including omission or use that differs from English.
Use the contractions del and al.
Use demonstrative adjectives este, esta, ese, esa and their plurals with agreement.
Use indefinite adjectives cada, mismo, otro, todo, and the forms algún and ningún.
Use possessive adjectives mi, tu, su, nuestro, vuestro with agreement.
Use subject pronouns, normally omitting them except for change of subject or emphasis.
Place direct object pronouns before verbs, on infinitives, or on commands.
Place indirect object pronouns correctly in one- and two-verb constructions.
Place singular reflexive pronouns in one- and two-verb constructions.
Use plural reflexive pronouns, including reciprocal meaning.
Use interrogative pronouns cuál, cuánto, quién with agreement.
Use the relative pronoun que in subject relative clauses.
Use esto and eso, and the pronouns alguno and ninguno.
Place negatives no, nada, nunca, nadie, ninguno correctly in the sentence.
Ask questions by intonation or with question words followed by verb then subject.
Conjugate regular -ar, -er, -ir verbs in the present, for simple and ongoing meaning.
Use the five stem-change and spelling clusters: encontrar, pensar, pedir, conocer, poner.
Use irregular present forms of estar, hacer, ir, ser, tener, including tener expressions like tener frío.
Form the present continuous with estar plus present participle.
Use the preterite for completed past events, with regular verbs.
Use the irregular preterite of ir, ser, dar and the irregular stems such as tuve, hice, quise.
Form the present perfect with haber plus past participle, including irregular participles.
Form the near future with ir a plus infinitive.
Use the imperfect for habitual and ongoing past, in the singular, with era, iba, veía.
Use the imperfect continuous with estar plus present participle.
Form the inflectional future, including tendr-, har-, podr-, pondr- and habrá.
Form the conditional, including the same irregular stems and habría.
Give affirmative tú commands, including irregulars sé, ve, ten, ven, haz, di, pon, sal.
Use interesar-type verbs with their object-verb-subject word order.
Use deber, poder, querer, tener que, saber plus infinitive, and quisiera or me gustaría plus infinitive.
Use reflexive verbs in all persons, singular and plural.
Use hay, hay que, impersonal se puede/se necesita and hace plus weather noun.
Make adjectives agree in gender and number following regular patterns.
Use nationality adjectives ending in a consonant, e.g. francés, español.
Place adjectives mostly after the noun, with set prenominal adjectives such as buen, gran, primer.
Distinguish ser and estar with adjectives, including meaning changes.
Use menos...que and the irregular comparatives mejor and peor.
Position adverbs of time, manner and place.
Use más...que/de, menos...que/de, tan...como with mejor and peor.
Use the personal a and de for possession.
Use para and sin plus infinitive, and antes de and después de plus infinitive.
Use prepositions required after verbs, noting when they change meaning.
Recognise diminutive -ito/-ita and intensive -ísimo/-ísima.
Recognise adverbs in -mente, nouns in -idad and adjectives in -able.
Use the demonstrative aquel with agreement.
Place nos and os object and plural reflexive pronouns correctly.
Use relative pronouns lo que, el que, el cual, and cuando, donde, que in relative clauses.
Use possessive pronouns el mío, el tuyo, el suyo, el nuestro, el vuestro, and aquello.
Use pronouns after prepositions, conmigo, contigo and emphatic a plus pronoun.
Use ya no, tampoco, ni...ni... in negative sentences.
Use the future and conditional in plural forms, including saber, querer, venir, decir, salir irregular stems.
Use the imperfect in plural forms including ir, ser, ver.
Apply spelling and stem changes in the preterite and participles as credit-bearing features.
Give affirmative commands in tú and vosotros forms.
Use the present subjunctive of hacer, ser, ir, venir, tener after cuando for the future.
Use the present subjunctive after verbs of wishing, command, request and emotion plus que.
Use the present subjunctive after para que to express purpose.
Use acabar de plus infinitive for having just done something.
Form the passive with ser plus participle plus por, or with se.
Use seguir and llevar plus present participle for ongoing actions.
Use the present with desde hace for actions continuing from the past.
Understand impersonal verbs parece, basta, falta, hace falta, vale la pena.
Use lo plus adjective as a noun, e.g. lo bueno.
Use post-verbal possessive adjectives mío, tuyo, suyo, nuestro, vuestro.
Form regular superlative adjectives and adverbs, including el mejor and el peor.
Pronounce Spanish vowels a, e, i, o, u clearly and consistently.
Know sounds of ll, ch, ñ, j, v, h (silent) and the r and rr sounds.
Read c and g before a/o/u versus e/i, and qu, gu, gue, gui, z correctly when speaking and writing.
Stress any vowel carrying a written accent when reading aloud.
Apply the default stress rule: penultimate syllable for words ending in vowel, n or s; otherwise final.
Place written accents correctly when transcribing, including antepenultimate stress.
Learn the Foundation list of 1,200 items for listening, speaking, reading and writing.
Learn the extra 500 Higher items, plus phrases and cultural place names.
Know regularly inflected and (in Reading) regularly derived forms of listed words.
Use words with several meanings or parts of speech, knowing every English equivalent.
